chunks.text: Step-by-Step Election Day Voting Procedure Polling units open nationwide at 8:30 AM. Accreditation and voting commence simultaneously and conclude at 2:30 PM. However, every voter on the queue on or before 2:30 PM is entitled to vote. Join the Orderly Queue: Arrive at your registered Polling Unit and join the orderly queue. Ensure you have your physical Permanent Voter Card (PVC) with you. Present Your PVC: Present your Permanent Voter Card (PVC) to the Assistant Presiding Officer (APO II) who scans the card details on the BVAS reader. BVAS Biometric Accreditation: The BVAS captures and verifies your fingerprint biometrics. If fingerprint capture fails, facial recognition authentication is instantly deployed. Register Check & Ballot Paper: The Assistant Presiding Officer (APO I) verifies your name on the register, marks the register, signs and stamps the official ballot paper, and hands it to you. Thumbprint in Secret: Proceed to the private voting cubicle.

Constitutional Rights & Civic Duties of the Nigerian Voter

Under the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended) and the Electoral Act 2022, every Nigerian citizen possesses distinct civic rights alongside obligations necessary for transparent and peaceful democratic governance.
chunks.section: Constitutional Rights & Civic Duties of the Nigerian Voter

chunks.text:
Your Constitutional Rights

Right to Vote & Be Voted For: Eligible citizens who satisfy statutory requirements have the unalienable right to register, vote at elections, and stand for elective office via sponsored political parties.

Right to Ballot Secrecy (Privacy): You have the absolute right to mark your ballot paper in complete secrecy inside the polling booth without fear of intimidation or surveillance.

Right to Recall an Elected Representative: Registered voters in any constituency retain the legal power under Section 69 and 110 of the 1999 Constitution to recall an elected legislator who fails to represent them.

Right to Information & Voter Education: Citizens are entitled to accessible, timely, and impartial voter education and clear guidelines published by INEC across all communication platforms.

Your Civic Responsibilities

Early Registration & Safe Custody of PVC: Ensure timely registration during Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) and safeguard your Permanent Voter Card against loss or damage.

Orderly Conduct on Election Day: Maintain peaceful and disciplined conduct, obey queue rules, respect election officials and security personnel, and refrain from inciting unrest.

Refusal of Vote Buying / Selling: Resist all forms of financial bribery, inducement, or material promises in exchange for votes. Vote according to your conscience and conviction.

Assisting Vulnerable Citizens: Grant priority and respectful assistance to pregnant women, nursing mothers, the elderly, and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) at the polling booth.

Gender Mainstreaming & Civil Society Inclusivity

The Commission is firmly dedicated to ensuring full, safe, and active participation of Nigerian women, youth, marginalized communities, and Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in all phases of the democratic process.

INEC Gender Policy (2021-2025): Institutionalized frameworks aligning with the National Gender Policy 2006 and UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to eliminate systemic barriers against female political participation.

Mitigation of Violence Against Women: Joint training workshops with UN Women and security sector agencies across all six geopolitical zones to establish dedicated Gender Units protecting female voters and candidates.

Inclusion for PWDs & The Leprosy Mission: Deployment of Braille ballot guides for visually impaired citizens, magnifying glasses for albinism voters, and accessible polling booth pathways across the country.

Electoral Offences and Prescribed Penalties

The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended) and the Electoral Act 2022 prescribe severe sanctions, hefty fines, and compulsory prison sentences for offences committed before, during, or after elections.

Offence: Vote Buying & Bribery
Penalty: ₦500,000 fine or 12 months imprisonment (or both).

Offence: Multiple Registration
Penalty: ₦100,000 fine or 12 months imprisonment (or both).

Offence: Snatching Ballot Box / BVAS
Penalty: 24 months imprisonment without option of fine.

Offence: Possession of Offensive Weapons
Penalty: ₦500,000 fine or 3 years imprisonment (or both).

Offence: Impersonation & Voting Twice
Penalty: ₦500,000 fine or 12 months imprisonment.

Offence: Campaigning on Election Day
Penalty: ₦100,000 fine or 6 months imprisonment.

chunks.text:
Collation & Declaration of Results Framework

Collation is the transparent arithmetic summation of votes cast at elections across statutory tiers, culminating in the mandatory Declaration of Results by designated Returning Officers.

Polling Unit (PU): Ballots counted openly; Form EC8A signed & uploaded to IReV portal.

Registration Area / Ward: RA Collation Officer sums all PUs in the ward; declares Councillorship.

Local Government Area (LGA): LGA Collation Officer sums all wards; declares LGA Chairmanship.

Constituency & Senatorial: Returning Officers declare State/Federal Assembly and Senate winners.

Presidential Election Threshold

Under Section 133 of the 1999 Constitution, to be declared winner, a presidential candidate must score:
- The highest number of valid votes cast nationwide; and
- Not less than 25% of votes cast in at least two-thirds (24) of all 36 States and the FCT, Abuja.
Governorship & Assembly Thresholds

For state executive and legislative races:
- Governorship: Highest total votes + at least 25% in two-thirds of all LGAs in the State.
- National & State Assembly: Simple majority of valid votes cast in the constituency.
